items.note: The skip_specs: true exception in .openspec.yaml cannot be observed, so this item does not apply it.

sources.quote: Create specification files that define WHAT the system should do.
Create one spec file per capability listed in the proposal's Capabilities section.

items.downgrade_reason: The rule covers only newly introduced segments. The pattern checks every spec path, including existing modified-capability paths that might not be kebab-case.

sources.quote: Any path segment newly introduced in the proposal must be kebab-case.

items.note: This needs to compare the depth of new spec paths with the layout of the existing openspec/specs tree. No available kind can do that.

sources.quote: Follow the project's existing organization; do not add a new domain level when the project uses a flat layout.

items.note: This needs a mapping of modified-capability delta paths to existing main spec paths. No selector can separate modified capabilities from new ones.

sources.quote: Modified capabilities: use the exact existing path from `openspec/specs/<capability-path>/` when creating the delta at `specs/<capability-path>/spec.md`.

items.note: Moving or renaming an existing capability means a write under openspec/specs/. During ff, the change should only write delta specs under changes/.

sources.quote: Do not move or rename the capability.

items.note: This needs a per-file write sequence, with one spec file per write call and no batched writes. No available kind checks this.

sources.quote: Write the spec files one at a time, so the user sees progress and an interrupted run keeps the files it already wrote:

items.note: This resume behaviour needs to know which spec files existed before the stage and which capability was written first. No available kind expresses that.

sources.quote: Before writing anything, compare the capabilities the proposal lists with the `specs/<capability-path>/spec.md` files that already exist, and start with the first capability that has no file.

items.note: source_write covers only files that existed at BASE_SHA, which matches 'an existing file'.

sources.quote: with the `specs/<capability-path>/spec.md` files that already exist, ... Do not rewrite an existing file unless the user asks you to.
Stop when every capability the proposal lists has its file.

items.downgrade_reason: This is inferred: at least one spec file means the proposal must declare at least one capability. The skip_specs exception cannot be observed, so the item does not apply it.
items.note: The spec-file existence check itself is already covered by the schema-026 artifact_exists item.

sources.quote: There must be at least one spec file unless the change's `.openspec.yaml` sets `skip_specs: true` ... If the proposal lists no capabilities and `skip_specs` is not set, revisit the proposal first.

unitemized.reason: This is guidance on what good spec content looks like (observable behaviour, inputs and outputs, constraints, testable scenarios). It is a quality judgment. Checking for scenario headings would need a literal that is not in the cited lines, and the spec template was not provided.
'Preserve the full path' is checked through schema-031 (openspec.capabilities listed_have_specs compares the exact capability paths) and schema-036.
This duplicates schema-031: the listed_have_specs rule already checks that each listed capability has a spec file at its exact path.
The rule applies only when the change modifies an existing capability. The reference language has no observable predicate for that, so no applies_when can be written.
The rule depends on whether a registered standalone store exists. That cannot be observed, so it is not itemized.
